## n8n vs Zapier

**Pricing model difference:** n8n counts an entire workflow execution as 1
execution regardless of node count. Zapier counts each step as a separate task
[15][16]. This makes n8n significantly cheaper for multi-step, high-volume
workflows.

| Aspect | n8n | Zapier |
|--------|-----|--------|
| Free tier | Self-hosted unlimited [15] | 100 tasks/month, 5 Zaps [16] |
| Paid entry | $24/month (2,500 executions) [9] | $19.99/month (750 tasks) [16] |
| Self-hosted cost | $5-10/month infrastructure [9] | Not available [15] |
| Code support | JavaScript + Python nodes [40] | Limited code [16] |
| Integration count | 400+ built-in, 5,800+ community [8] | 7,000+ [15] |

**Key differentiator:** Every Zapier integration has an n8n equivalent via
native node, community node, or HTTP Request node [16]. n8n targets
developers/technical teams; Zapier targets non-technical users [16].

## n8n vs Make (Integromat)

| Aspect | n8n | Make |
|--------|-----|------|
| UI philosophy | Visual + code balanced [18] | Visual simplicity [18] |
| Execution counting | Full workflow = 1 [17] | Each module = 1 operation [17] |
| Self-hosting | Yes [18] | Cloud-only [18] |
| AI capabilities | "Decisively ahead" [17] | AI Agents added April 2025 [17] |
| Target | Developers, mixed teams [18] | Operations, marketers [18] |

Make wins for fastest setup, visual clarity, and non-technical teams. n8n wins
for self-hosting, custom code, AI-heavy automations, and cost at scale [17][18].

## n8n vs Temporal

| Aspect | n8n | Temporal |
|--------|-----|---------|
| Architecture | Queue-based (main + workers) [8] | Microservices (4 services via gRPC) [8] |
| State persistence | Database records, manual resume [8] | Event history replay, auto reconstruction [8] |
| Recovery | Manual retry from failure point [8] | Automatic with exact state [8] |
| Resource needs | Single container + 256MB [8] | Min 4 containers + 4GB RAM [8] |
| Failure handling | Node-level retry + Error Trigger [8] | Auto exponential backoff [8] |
| Version control | JSON workflows (harder) [8] | Code-first (natural Git) [8] |
| Integrations | 400+ built-in + 5,800 community [8] | 7 language SDKs [8] |
| Cloud pricing | $24/month [9] | $100/month [8] |
| Event limit | No hard limit [8] | 51,200 per execution [8] |

**When to choose:** n8n for business automation, SaaS API integration, visual
workflows. Temporal for distributed systems needing transactional integrity and
long-running services [8]. Some teams use both together [8].

## n8n vs Windmill

| Aspect | n8n | Windmill |
|--------|-----|----------|
| License | Sustainable Use [14] | AGPLv3 (open-source) [19] |
| Philosophy | Visual-first, optional code [3] | Code-first, scripts as workflows [19] |
| Languages | JavaScript (+ Python in Code node) [40] | 20+ languages [10] |
| Dependency management | Pre-installed required [10] | Per-node management [10] |
| Pre-built integrations | 400+ [8] | Fewer, more custom [19] |
| Performance | Standard Node.js [3] | Claims zero overhead vs bare-metal [10] |

Windmill is positioned for engineering teams wanting Git-based workflows. n8n
for mixed teams with non-technical members [19].

## n8n vs Apache Airflow

| Aspect | n8n | Airflow |
|--------|-----|---------|
| Purpose | Business process automation [20] | Data pipelines/ETL at scale [20] |
| Interface | Visual drag-and-drop [3] | Code-only (Python DAGs) [20] |
| Technical bar | No programming required [3] | Python expertise required [20] |
| Maturity | Newer, maturing [20] | Battle-tested (Airbnb, Google, Netflix) [20] |
| Best for | App connections, business glue [20] | ML pipelines, complex dependencies [20] |

Some organizations use both: Airflow for data engineering, n8n for
operations/marketing automation [20].

## n8n vs Prefect

Prefect positions as "modern Airflow" (launched 2018). Python-native with hybrid
execution model (cloud + local). Simpler than Airflow for basic pipelines [64].
Limited direct n8n-vs-Prefect comparison sources; most Prefect comparisons focus
on Airflow [64].
